$comment: Primary-source oracle — survivor / dual-entitlement cases: SSA POMS RS 00615.020 separate-reduction composition and the RS 00615.320 RIB-LIM cap. Expected values derived independently from the cited sources; never from production code.

poms-rs-00615-020.name: SSA POMS RS 00615.020 — Dual Entitlement Overview
poms-rs-00615-020.identifier: Method C worked example: spouse benefit $1,000 / RIB $400 before reduction -> full RIB subtracted from full spouse benefit, the $600 excess reduced separately to $540, RIB reduced to $380, total payable $920

poms-reduction-rates.name: SSA POMS RS 00615.101 (Reduced RIB) + RS 00615.201 (Reduced Spouse's Benefits) — 42 U.S.C. §402(q) actuarial reduction rates
poms-reduction-rates.identifier: Worker (RIB) reduction 5/9 of 1% per month for the first 36 early months, 5/12 of 1% beyond; spousal reduction 25/36 of 1% per month for the first 36, 5/12 of 1% beyond

poms-rs-00615-320.name: SSA POMS RS 00615.320 — Reduced WIB, deceased NH entitled to reduced RIB (RIB-LIM)
poms-rs-00615-320.identifier: Widow(er) benefit limited to the LARGER of 82 1/2 percent of the deceased's PIA and the deceased's own reduced benefit

cases.description: The POMS RS 00615.020 Method C worked example, reproduced by the independent separate-reduction composition formula (workbook-only case — the POMS illustration factors are given, not derived from claim ages).
cases.tolerance: exact (the POMS worked example's own dollars)
derivation: POMS gives: spouse benefit $1,000 and RIB $400 before reduction; the RIB reduces to $380 (implied factor 0.95) and the $600 excess reduces to $540 (implied factor 0.90).
The incorrect larger-of method (max of reduced RIB and reduced whole spouse benefit = max(380, 900)) yields 900, not the POMS-published 920 — the composition, not the max, is the law.

cases.description: Dual entitlement at age 62 (both FRA 67): reduced own benefit PLUS the separately-reduced spousal excess.
derivation: Recipient PIA $800, worker PIA $2,000; both claim at 62y0m = 60 months early (FRA 67).
Spousal excess = max(0, 0.5*2,000 - 800) = 200/mo, reduced by the SPOUSAL schedule: 36*(25/3600) + 24*(5/1200) = 35% -> 200*0.65 = 130.00/mo -> annual 1,560.
Total = 8,280/yr. The incorrect larger-of method gives max(6,720, 0.65*1,000*12 = 7,800) = 7,800 — $480/yr low.

cases.description: RIB-LIM: the deceased claimed at 62 (reduced RIB $1,400); the survivor claims at survivor FRA. The widow benefit caps at the larger of 82.5% of PIA and the deceased's reduced benefit.
derivation: Deceased: PIA $2,000, FRA 67 (804 months), claimed at 744 months (62y0m) -> reduced RIB = 2,000*(1-0.30) = 1,400; died Dec 31 2030 (age 823 months at the Jan-1-2031 boundary).
Survivor claims the survivor benefit at their survivor FRA (804 months, April 2031) -> no widow(er) early reduction (factor 1.0).
Widow base = full PIA 2,000 (the deceased's own early reduction never flows into the widow base).
RIB-LIM (POMS RS 00615.320): deceased was entitled to a reduced RIB before death -> cap at max(0.825*2,000 = 1,650, 1,400) = 1,650.
Widow monthly = min(2,000, 1,650) = 1,650 -> annual 19,800 (no COLA: evaluation year equals the deceased's COLA anchor year).
